title: Frontline quirk docket + mini-solution sketches
content:
Purpose: quick stash of small but recurrent customer frictions collected during Q1 account check-ins. These are frontline oddities ("quirks") rather than scoped feature epics. For each item: one-line symptom, representative quote, measured signal (where available), risk/impact guess, and 1–2 low-effort probe sketches we can ship in a sprint.

Context notes:
- Observations pulled from CS call logs (Mar 2026), SRE incident notes, and a 15-minute sync with Solutions Engineering (4/6).
- Prioritization here is intentionally opportunistic: high ROI where engineering effort is small or where a config/console tweak unlocks value.
- We will run 2-week microprobes for top 3 items, instrumenting success metrics (error reduction, customer happiness tag, retention banners) and reporting back to product and SRE.

Items:
1) "Dropped streaming chunks" — intermittent stream terminates with 200 but missing tokens
   - Quote: "We see streaming stop mid reply — the client thinks it's done but tokens keep buffering on our side." (Strategic AI startup, multi-tenant Hosted API)
   - Signal: 12% of streaming sessions in last 30d where chunk gap > 3s; 3 P0 tickets in March.
   - Impact: User-facing incomplete replies, increased re-querying, cost inflation.
   - Quick probes:
     a) Add a small client-side heuristic: if stream silent >2.5s and server returned 200, show "response pending, reconnecting" banner (SDK change, low-risk).
     b) Server-side metric and alert for "stream closed with partial token buffer" to correlate with transport errors (SRE + runtime instrumentation).
   - Success metric: reduce customer re-query events by 40% within 2 weeks.

2) "Embedding variance across model versions" — customers surprised by shifts after auto-rollouts
   - Quote: "Our similarity indices jumped after the model update; we had to re-index to get expected behavior." (Enterprise search customer)
   - Signal: 5 customers reported drift within 7 days of model-matrix rollouts (Apr).
   - Impact: downstream embedding indices and retrieval pipelines break silently.
   - Quick probes:
     a) Add a simple "post-rollout drift alert" email for customers with persistent embedding-usage (threshold delta on cosine distributions).
     b) Console toggle to opt out of auto-rollouts for embedding-critical endpoints (UI + API flag) — quick guardrail.
   - Success metric: zero surprise escalations for enrolled customers during next known rollout event.

3) "Quota confusion for dedicated vs hosted" — teams misinterpret per-project quotas
   - Quote: "We expected Dedicated reservations to be isolated but our test tokens were still billed to hosted project quotas." (mid-market customer on Dedicated trial)
   - Signal: 2 billing disputes and 1 onboarding delay last quarter.
   - Impact: Sales friction for Dedicated upsell, churn risk for pilots.
   - Quick probes:
     a) Inline console explainer card when creating Dedicated pools: "Billing isolation checklist" (copy + CTA to support).
     b) Small SDK helper: warn if API key used in Hosted project is associated with Dedicated reservation mismatch.
   - Success metric: zero billing-dispute follow-ups in next pilot cohort.

4) "Tool-calling finicky inputs" — customers hit parsing errors when functions return slightly different shapes
   - Quote: "When our tool returns an empty array instead of null, the agent halts and logs a 'shape mismatch' error." (platform engineering team)
   - Signal: repeated errors in logs during synthetic tool tests; recurrent Slack thread.
   - Impact: Breaks agent workflows; increased engineer time to debug.
   - Quick probes:
     a) Make function-call parsing tolerant to common shape variants (empty array vs null vs missing key) for 3 most-used SDK languages (JS/Python/Go).
     b) Publish a short "Tool shape troubleshooting" one-pager in Console docs and a post-call SDK helper to normalize outputs.
   - Success metric: reduce 'shape mismatch' agent errors by 70% for customers using tool-calls in-staging.

5) "Opaque latency spikes on multi-tenant bursts" — customers see throughput regressions during noisy neighbors
   - Quote: "During our busy hours latency jumped 2x; it's hard to tell if it's our workload or platform throttling." (SaaS analytics customer)
   - Signal: 3 correlated incidents where requests routed to different capacity tiers; some traced to autoscale cold starts.
   - Impact: SLA embarrassment; engineering time chasing root cause.
   - Quick probes:
     a) Small Console heatmap showing per-tenant tail-latency percentiles over last 24h (expose routing tier + cold-start events).
     b) Add attribution metadata to traces indicating routing decision (tier/queue/quantization) so customer teams can see why a request hit a slower path.
   - Success metric: customers can self-diagnose 80% of latency spike cases without raising CS tickets.

6) "Confusing rollouts UX for experiments" — teams want canary + quick rollback but find the UI cumbersome
   - Quote: "I tried a canary split and couldn't stop it quickly — had to open a ticket." (growth PM)
   - Signal: documented friction logs in three different PM teams; manual rollback takes 45m avg.
   - Impact: risk-averse orgs avoid experimenting; slower iteration.
   - Quick probes:
     a) One-click 'pause canary' button that instantly flips traffic to baseline while preserving config (frontend + backend toggle).
     b) Add a 'guardrail' that surfaces potential incompatibilities before canary starts (model mismatch, quantization incompatible flags).
   - Success metric: average rollback time <5m for paused canaries in next 30-day run.

Open questions + unknowns:
- How many customers would enable a Console "opt-out of auto-embedding-rollouts" vs prefer email alerts? (estimate: 20–40% enterprise customers)
- Any SRE concerns with adding extra routing metadata to traces (privacy/perf tradeoffs)? Need SRE sign-off.
- Is SDK-level streaming heuristic acceptable as long as server keeps authoritative replay logs? Legal wants to avoid 'best-effort' promises in docs.

Next steps (short):
- Prioritize top 3 items for 2-week probes: Streaming chunks (#1), Embedding rollouts (#2), Dedicated billing UX (#3).
- Lina to scope SDK banner and console card (ETA 4/22).
- Benji + SRE to add server-side streaming gap metric and an alert (ETA 4/20).
- Diego to prototype embedding drift email and console toggle (ETA 4/24).
- Aisha to set up instrumentation dashboard template and shared measurement doc (ETA 4/16).

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Track conversions: "probe -> rollback -> fix" pipeline, separate telemetry for probe cohorts.
- Keep solutions low-friction: avoid new infra on first pass; prefer SDK/console/alerting changes.
- Flag anything that grows into 3+ engineering weeks as an "feature" and move to product planning.

Attachments / raw references:
- Call notes snippets: CS-Calls-2026-03-15-04-29 (internal doc ref)
- Incident traces: SRE-STREAM-INC-0326 (SRE ticket)
- Customer quotes anonymized in linked_artifacts above.

If this resonates, I can convert top-3 probes into JIRA cards with acceptance criteria and lightweight telemetry checklists.
